title: Tiered prefetch throttle + eviction-score desync — playbook and longterm mitigations
creator: Priya Shah
description: Follow-up ticket after a production capacity event where a combination of aggressive tenant-prefetch heuristics and a recently-introduced eviction score recalculation race led to persistent ghost entries and a slow-growing memory leak in the prefix/KV cache. This ticket scopes short-term mitigations (playbook) and longer-term fixes to prevent recurrence and reduce blast radius.
incident_summary: On 2026-02-18, multiple clusters experienced progressive memory growth over 6–10 hours resulting in capacity pressure and degraded tail latency. Root investigation showed tenant-scoped prefetches were issuing speculative inserts while an eviction-score recalculation optimization (merged in runtime-2.3.6) could leave entries in a ephemeral state not visible to normal lookup paths but retained by slab allocators. Combined with high write burst from a customer workload, the slab population never reclaimed certain entries and compaction failed to sweep them.
impact: Several Dedicated pools hit >85% memory utilization; autoscaler triggered node replacement causing request latency spikes and retry storms. Two enterprise customers reported transient 503s and increased token costs due to retries. No customer data was exposed.
timeline: 2026-02-18 02:12 UTC - first memory spike alerted; 2026-02-18 03:05 UTC - mitigation: throttle tenant prefetches cluster-wide (manual flag); 2026-02-18 05:30 UTC - rolling restart of affected nodes; 2026-02-18 10:40 UTC - memory utilization stabilized; 2026-02-19 - investigation begins; 2026-02-27 - root cause hypothesis finalized; 2026-03-10 - this follow-up ticket created.
root_cause: A race between prefetch insertion path and new eviction-score recalculation produced entries where the 'live' bit was never atomically set in the primary prefix index, but slabs retained the allocation. The async compaction path assumed all index mutations were canonical and skipped tombstones with missing live bits, leaving allocations orphaned. High prefetch rates amplified the effect into a memory growth condition.
investigation_notes:
- Heap/Slab traces captured from two clusters show identical allocation shapes and a consistent prefix hash range.
- Reproduced locally with a synthetic tenant generator that issues high fanout prefetches and concurrent eviction-score recalculations.
- The eviction-score change attempted to batch score updates to reduce CPU; its batching window could reorder tombstone application relative to an insert path.
- Existing checksum alerts didn't fire because the orphaned slabs still had valid metadata; only index liveness was inconsistent.
decisions:
- Short-term: enable a conservative prefetch throttle, add index liveness assertions in debug builds, and augment compaction to detect and reclaim orphaned slabs.
- Mid-term: revert the non-essential batching in eviction-score recalculation until we add atomic index-update primitives.
- Long-term: redesign prefix index mutation model to be crash-consistent and introduce periodic full-index reconciliation job with low-cost sampling.

A4: Add end-to-end integration test that simulates concurrent prefetch + eviction updates, run in CI with stress gate — owner: Priya Shah — due: 2026-03-24
A5: Instrument and add alert: 'kvcache.index-liveness-fraction < 0.995' to postmortem dashboard and on-call runbook — owner: SRE Team (contact: Anika Patel) — due: 2026-03-18
A6: Create tenant-level backpressure policy to limit speculative prefetch fanout when memory > 70% — owner: Platform Team (contact: Marco Alvarez) — due: 2026-03-31

runbook_changes: Add step: if kvcache memory grows >10% in 1h, enable 'prefetch.cluster_throttle' and open ENG-incident-channel;
Add step: when orphan_reclaims > 0 for >3 hours, schedule rolling restart of affected nodes after compaction patch is deployed.
